messages.subject: Stochastic Gompertz state space model
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to get some state space models running in INLA. So far I have a stochastic level (random walk with noise) model going and a stochastic level with drift (random walk with drift) model going. I am trying to take it one more step to get a stochastic Gompertz model running but can't figure it out. Any help is appreciated. Code is below.

Thanks, Tim

#### libraries
library(INLA); library(brinla)

#### make and plot data
n = 50; m <- n-1; x0 = 20
W = 0.3; V = 0.3;
d0 = 5; d1 = -0.3
w  = rnorm(n, 0, W); v  = rnorm(n, 0, V)
x = y = rep(0, n)
x[1] = x0 + w[1]
y[1] = x[1] +       v[1]
for (t in 2:n){
  x[t] = x[t-1] + d0 + d1*x[t-1] + w[t]
  y[t] = x[t]   +         v[t]
}
plot(y,type="l",xlab="time",ylab=""); lines(x,col=2)
legend("topright",legend=c("y","x"), col=c("black", "red"),
       lty=c(1,1), bty="n")

#### create y matrix for augmented model
Y <- matrix(NA, n+m, 2)
Y[1:n,     1] <- y              
Y[1:m + n, 2] <- 0              

#### indices and weights
i  <- c(1:n, 2:n)              # indices for  the states x_t
j  <- c(rep(NA,n), 2:n -1)     # indices for x_{t-1}
wj <- c(rep(NA,n), rep(-1,m))  # weights for x_{t-1}
l  <- c(rep(NA,n), 2:n)        # indices for the perturbation terms w_t
wl <- c(rep(NA,n), rep(-1,m))  # weights for w_t
d0 <- c(rep(NA,n), rep(-1,m))  # constant drift

#### stochastic level model
# x_t = x_{t-1} + w_t         where w_t ~ N(0, W)
# 0 = x_t - x_{t-1} - w_t     where w_t ~ N(0, W)
formula1 <- Y ~ -1 +
  f(i, model="iid", initial=-10, fixed=T) + # x_t
  f(j, wj, copy="i") + # x_{t-1}
  f(l, wl, model ="iid") # perterbations w_t
r1 <- inla(formula1, data = data.frame(i, j, wj, l, wl, d0),
           family = rep("gaussian", 2),
           control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
           control.compute = list(waic=T))
summary(r1)
bri.hyperpar.summary(r1)
plot(y); lines(r1$summary.random$i$mean)
r1$waic$waic

#### stochastic level with drift, d0, model
# x_t = x_{t-1} + d0 + w_t        where w_t ~ N(0, W)
# 0 = x_t - x_{t-1} - d0 - w_t    where w_t ~ N(0, W)
formula2 <- Y ~ -1 +
  f(i, model="iid", initial=-10, fixed=T) + # x_t
  f(j, wj, copy="i") + # x_{t-1}
  f(l, wl, model ="iid") + # perterbations w_t
  d0 # drift constant?
r2 <- inla(formula2, data = data.frame(i, j, wj, wl, l, d0),
           family = rep("gaussian", 2),
           control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
           control.compute = list(waic=T))
summary(r2)
bri.hyperpar.summary(r2)
plot(y); lines(r2$summary.random$i$mean)
r2$waic$waic

#### stochastic gompertz with baseline growth, d0, and growth penalty, d1
# x_t = x_{t-1} + d0 + d1*x_{t-1} + w_t       where w_t ~ N(0, W)
# 0 = x_t - x_{t-1} - d0 - d1*x_{t-1} - w_t     where w_t ~ N(0, W)

# additional indices or weights?
k <-
wk <-
 
# new formula?
formula3 <- Y ~ -1 +

# compute?
r3 <- inla(formula3, data = data.frame(i, j, wj, wl, l, d0), # add more inputs?
           family = rep("gaussian", 2),
           control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE),
           control.compute = list(waic=T))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Stochastic Gompertz state space model
parts:
you can have more than one copy (of the same effect) in the formula

f(time,...) + 
f(time1, w.neg.one, copy="time") + 
f(time2, w.neg.one, copy="time",
hyper=list(beta=list(fixed=FALSE)) ## to get 'd1'

assuming t=1...n, then

time=1:n
time1=c(NA, 1:(n-1))
time2=time1
w.neg.one=rep(-1,n)


but you can also join x_{t-1} and d1*x_{t-1} if you like, even if you
know the sign of 'd1', as you can define an interval for the scaling in
copy via range=c(low,high) argument,


range: A vector of size two giving the lower and upper range for the
scaling parameter ‘beta’ in the model ‘COPY’, ‘CLINEAR’,
‘MEC’ and ‘MEB’. If ‘low = high’ then the identity mapping is
used.

> # 0 = x_t - x_{t-1} - d0 - d1*x_{t-1} - w_t     where w_t ~ N(0, W)
> >

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Stochastic Gompertz state space model
parts:
x_t can only be indexed from 2 to 50, and x_{t-1} from 1 to 49.
If you want to directly involve x_1 you'll need to work out some kind
of "initial distribution" for that; for stationary AR(1) processes
without drift that's well defined (and what INLA does internally), but
when you have drift there's no clear "right way".
The easiest solution is to not involve that in the likelihood, and
instead only involve the fully defined pairs.

Finn
